Retain also the source’s explicit support proof. Suppose a finite positive measure μ, continuous real ω and bounded function h, continuous on the closed upper half-plane and holomorphic inside, R eitω(q)dμ(q) and |h(z)| ≤C. For real b and ε > 0, integrate h(z)e−ibz−εz2 around satisfy h(t) = rectangles between heights 0, s. The vertical sides vanish as their real coordinates tend to infinity, with Gaussian bound proportional to e−εT 2. The horizontal Gaussian majorants are integrable, and Cauchy’s theorem gives
Z ≤C q h(t)e−ibt−εt2dt π/ε ebs+εs2. (PA1) R
